top5.text: Trump, Xi and Putin signed a four-point 'peace declaration' in Shenzhen on nuclear-risk talks, UN reform and fuel supply, with no arms-control deal.
Tusk and Sikorski rebuked Trump for calling Putin a friend; Tusk said US troops still anchor Polish security.
Belweder talks on fixing the Constitutional Tribunal stalled and were suspended; parties will send separate proposals next week.
Kraków council will hold an extraordinary session on 25 November over Gibała's halt to metro preparations.
Cyclone Akvan hit near Gopalpur, Odisha, early on Nov 20, weaker than feared; about 3 lakh people were evacuated.

US.text: Trump, Xi and Putin issued a four-point 'peace declaration' in Shenzhen, pledging nuclear-risk talks, UN reform and more refined-fuel supply, but no arms-control deal.
Anthropic opened at $111.50 in its Nasdaq debut but faded to close at $97.17, 17% above its $83 IPO price.
US.thread: Anthropic IPO and AI market valuations

US.text: S&P 500 fell 2% to 7,175.83, its sixth straight loss, and the Dow lost 1,101 points as Anthropic's debut failed to revive AI stocks.
The Senate rejected an Iran war-powers resolution 48-51, with three Republicans in favour and Fetterman and Tillis voting no.
The Ninth Circuit extended its stay on restoring Venezuelan TPS, so DOJ withdrew its Supreme Court bid. Terminations stay in effect pending a merits ruling.

Poland.text: Belweder talks on fixing the Constitutional Tribunal stalled and were suspended; parties are to send proposals next week, says Bogucki.
Sejm accepted 20 of 21 Senate amendments to the night alcohol-sales and advertising ban, rejecting only 0% beer ads; the law goes to Nawrocki.
Sejm passed the reimbursement reform 417–0, with a Critical Medicines List and cheaper Polish-made drugs from 2027; the Senate is next.
Sejm voted 403–8 to let up to 1.5bn zł of defence money fund chip production lines such as CEZAMAT; the bill goes to the Senate.
Short-term rental law, letting towns ban Airbnb-style lets in zones from 2028, passed its final Sejm stage and goes to the President.
ePUAP is fully restored after the Nov 10 cyberattack, the ministry says; no attacker has been named yet.

Kraków.text: Kraków council will hold an extraordinary session on 25 November at 16:00, called by KO and Nowa Lewica, over Gibała's halt to metro preparations.
Gibała wants a spring 2027 referendum on the SCT, short-term rentals, Main Square carriages and possibly small nuclear reactors; the council must agree and legality is disputed.
Kraków council voted 40 for, with 3 abstentions, on a resolution meant to stop commemoration of perpetrators of terror, including at burial sites.
Kraków council adopted 2026 budget amendments for current spending, including urgent repairs; details and vote counts not yet published.
Kraków.thread: Kraków city finances and the 2027 budget

city.text: Night works continue on the A4 Kraków bypass: the Kraków→Zabierzów link at Modlniczka is closed on the night of 20/21 Nov (and again 23/24, 24/25 Nov), with detours via S52 and Balice; Kraków Skawina slip roads close on rolling nights until 11 Dec, with a 110 km/h limit there.
The latest reading found (os. Piastów, 19 Nov 03:00) showed good air (AQI 29, low PM2.5/PM10); check GIOŚ for live levels as heating-season smog can build quickly in calm, foggy weather.
No current IMGW warning for Kraków was found in this check; mid-November brought repeated dense-fog warnings, so check IMGW before driving at night or early morning.
Today (Fri 20 Nov) from 8:30 the city gives away about 300 dahlias from its summer plantings on Plac św. Ducha, up to two per person while stocks last.
The free GEOGRAFICA travel festival of the Jagiellonian University's geography institute runs 20-21 Nov, with travel talks, national-park meetings and school workshops.

Trump shrugged off Tusk's criticism ('I can't do anything about it') and reportedly said Russian drones landed in Poland 'by mistake'.
PEJ and Westinghouse-Bechtel signed a letter of intent at P-TEC to order more long-lead parts for Poland's first nuclear plant; US to help on export-credit financing.

rules.name: Consumer Credit Directive 2 (CCD2)
rules.body: European Parliament and Council (Directive (EU) 2023/2225, CCD2); Polish implementing act not yet adopted
rules.changes: Brings many buy-now-pay-later, interest-free and small loans under full consumer-credit rules.
rules.affects: Borrowers, payday lenders, BNPL providers, online shops and banks in Poland.

rules.name: Anti-alcohol law: night sales ban (22:00–06:00) and alcohol advertising ban
rules.changes: Bans retail alcohol sales from 22:00 to 06:00, except in restaurants and bars, and lets municipalities widen the ban.
rules.affects: Shops, petrol stations, the alcohol and advertising industries, and consumers.

rules.name: Amendment to the reimbursement act (Critical Medicines List)
rules.body: Council of Ministers (Ministry of Health) / Sejm
rules.changes: Creates a national Critical Medicines List, raises the patient discount for Polish-made drugs from 15% to 30%, adds multi-criteria assessment for orphan drugs, a catalogue of equivalent therapies and spending caps, and drops OTC drugs from reimbursement.
rules.affects: Patients, pharmacies, drug makers, NFZ and hospitals.

rules.body: Commerce Department, Bureau of Industry and Security
rules.changes: Licence needed to supply advanced AI chips to data centres anywhere that give Chinese/Macau/D:5-headquartered firms more than 12m TPP of compute.
rules.affects: Chip exporters, cloud and data-centre operators worldwide (especially Southeast Asia), Chinese AI developers

rules.affects: Defence budget, universities, the chip industry

deepDive.title: Allies in step on hardware, out of step on Russia
deepDive.body:
**US–Poland.** The week showed two sides of the relationship. On security plumbing, things are moving. After meeting Pentagon policy chief Elbridge Colby on Nov 17, Defence Minister Kosiniak-Kamysz said the US force-posture review was nearly done and would reach the White House in early December, when Warsaw expects a decision on a permanent base. That follows the Nov 10 Statement of Intent on defence-industrial cooperation ([Breaking Defense](https://breakingdefense.com/2026/11/poland-says-pentagon-supports-permanent-us-base-with-decision-expected-in-december/)). At the P-TEC energy meeting, PEJ and Westinghouse-Bechtel signed a letter of intent on further nuclear components ([PEJ](https://pej.pl/en/press-center/news/pej-signed-a-letter-of-intent-with-the-westinghouse-bechtel-consortium-regarding-contracts-for-the-key-components-of-the-lubiatowo-kopalino-nuclear-power-plant/)). Politically, Trump calling Putin a 'friend' in Shenzhen drew unusually blunt replies from Tusk and Sikorski, and disapproval from the president's office ([Defence24](https://defence24.pl/geopolityka/politycy-reaguja-na-slowa-trumpa-o-putinie-boze-chron-nas)). Tusk was careful to describe US troops as a key guarantor of Polish security.

**US–India.** Security ties are steady and largely institutional. The Quad summit in Manila launched a maritime surveillance initiative, and the 23rd Military Cooperation Group met in Delhi on Nov 17–18. The Pannun case remains the main irritant: Nikhil Gupta's sentencing in New York on Nov 20 will put the alleged involvement of an Indian government employee back in the headlines. On trade, officials send mixed signals. The CEA talks of early December ([ANI](https://timesofoman.com/article/179355-worst-of-us-trade-friction-likely-behind-us-potential-december-deal-to-settle-ties-indias-cea-nageswaran)), while the Commerce Secretary ties signing to Washington's new tariff framework.

**Poland–India.** After Tusk's October visit, which set a goal of doubling trade by 2030 and opened a defence-industry dialogue, follow-through is slow. The classified-information agreement and WB Group's announced investment have not yet materialised.

*Analysis:* All three relationships are being built through bureaucratic and industrial channels, which so far have been insulated from leaders' rhetoric. The main test for Warsaw comes in early December. A base decision would show whether the Shenzhen-era warmth toward Moscow has any effect on US posture on NATO's eastern flank.
